question: Govind invested some money in HDFC at 4% per annum rate of interest. What would be the corresponding simple interest (in ₹) if after 2 years, Govind got ₹178.5 as compound interest, considering annual compounding?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For 2 years, the direct relation between Compound Interest (CI) and Simple Interest (SI) is:

CI = SI × (1 + R ÷ 200)

⇒ 178.5 = SI × (1 + 4 ÷ 200)

⇒ 178.5 = SI × 1.02

⇒ SI = 178.5 ÷ 1.02 = ₹175

**∴ The correct answer is ₹175.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Rate of interest (R) = 4% per annum

Time (T) = 2 years

Compound Interest (CI) = ₹178.5

**Formula Used:**

CI = P[(1 + R ÷ 100)T − 1]

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100
